title: Complex magnetic phase diagrams in Tb$_2$IrAl$_4$Ge$_2$ and Er$_2$IrAl$_4$Ge$_2$
authors: Karolina Gornicka, Matthew S. Cook, Brenden R. Ortiz, Andrew D. Christianson, Andrew F. May
abstract: We report the synthesis and comprehensive investigation of single-crystalline Tb$_2$IrAl$_4$Ge$_2$ and Er$_2$IrAl$_4$Ge$_2$, the first Ir-based members of the $Ln_2M$Al$_4$Ge$_2$ family. Both compounds crystallize in the tetragonal Tb$_2$NiAl$_4$Ge$_2$-type structure (space group $I4/mmm$) and exhibit easy-axis magnetic anisotropy with the crystallographic $c$ axis as the preferred magnetization direction. Tb$_2$IrAl$_4$Ge$_2$ undergoes antiferromagnetic ordering below $T_N = 25$ K and develops a sequence of field-induced metamagnetic transitions accompanied by pronounced magnetotransport anomalies, including a nonlinear Hall response. In contrast, Er$_2$IrAl$_4$Ge$_2$ exhibits three successive zero-field magnetic transitions and a substantially richer low-temperature magnetic phase diagram comprising multiple competing field-induced phases confined to relatively modest magnetic fields. The differences between the Tb- and Er-based compounds demonstrate the wide range of magnetic behavior that can be realized within the \ce{Tb2NiAl4Ge2}-type structure. More broadly, the successful realization of Ir-based $Ln_2M$Al$_4$Ge$_2$ compounds considerably expands the accessible chemical space of this family and opens a route toward the exploration of related $4d$- and $5d$-based aluminogermanides.
summary: This work reports on the synthesis and detailed magnetic characterization of $	ext{Tb}_2	ext{IrAl}_4	ext{Ge}_2$ and $	ext{Er}_2	ext{IrAl}_4	ext{Ge}_2$. The research reveals that the magnetic complexity increases substantially from the $	ext{Tb}$-based to the $	ext{Er}$-based compound, demonstrating a wide range of magnetic ground states within this structural family. This expands the known chemical space for studying correlated magnetism in $5d$-metal-based intermetallics.
main_problem: The study investigates the complex magnetic phase diagrams in the rare-earth intermetallic compounds $	ext{Tb}_2	ext{IrAl}_4	ext{Ge}_2$ and $	ext{Er}_2	ext{IrAl}_4	ext{Ge}_2$. The goal is to understand the magnetic behavior and expand the chemical space of the $	ext{Ln}_2	ext{MAl}_4	ext{Ge}_2$ family.
main_result: The compounds exhibit strong magnetic anisotropy with the $c$-axis as the easy direction. $	ext{Er}_2	ext{IrAl}_4	ext{Ge}_2$ shows a significantly richer and more complex low-temperature magnetic phase diagram with multiple competing field-induced phases compared to $	ext{Tb}_2	ext{IrAl}_4	ext{Ge}_2$.
method: The research employed comprehensive experimental techniques including single-crystal X-ray diffraction, magnetization measurements ($	ext{M}(T), 	ext{M}(H)$), heat capacity ($	ext{C}_p$), and magnetotransport measurements ($ho, 	ext{Hall}$ effect).
model_or_system: The physical system consists of single-crystalline $	ext{Tb}_2	ext{IrAl}_4	ext{Ge}_2$ and $	ext{Er}_2	ext{IrAl}_4	ext{Ge}_2$, which crystallize in the tetragonal $	ext{Tb}_2	ext{NiAl}_4	ext{Ge}_2$-type structure. The magnetic behavior is governed by the interplay between RKKY exchange interactions and Crystal-Electric-Field (CEF) effects.
key_observables: Magnetization ($	ext{M}$), magnetic transition temperatures ($T_N, T^*$), nonlinear Hall response, electrical resistivity ($ho$), and heat capacity ($	ext{C}_p$).
important_parameters: The magnetic anisotropy is strong, with the $c$-axis being the easy magnetization direction. The complexity increases significantly when moving from $	ext{Tb}$ to $	ext{Er}$ compounds.
main_assumptions: The magnetic coupling is assumed to be influenced by the localized $4f$ moments of the rare-earth elements interacting via RKKY exchange within the crystal structure.
figures_summary: The figures summarize $	ext{M}(T)$ and $	ext{M}(H)$ curves, showing the distinct magnetic transitions for both compounds, and magnetotransport data illustrating the coupling between charge transport and magnetic order.
paper_structure: The paper details the synthesis and structural characterization of the single crystals, followed by a systematic presentation of magnetic measurements ($	ext{M}(T), 	ext{M}(H)$) revealing the distinct phase diagrams for $	ext{Tb}$ and $	ext{Er}$ compounds, and concluding with a discussion on the implications for the $	ext{Ln}_2	ext{MAl}_4	ext{Ge}_2$ family.
why_interesting: The study of complex magnetic phase diagrams in strongly correlated materials like these aluminogermanides provides a rich platform for understanding competing magnetic interactions, which is relevant to many-body physics and frustrated magnetism.
